# function: mode_to_octal

Converts a file mode to the four-digit octal form, such as `"0644"`, that the `mode` attributes of this provider accept and report, so that modes written in different ways can be compared or passed on. It accepts:

- Octal modes, as the `mode` attributes do: `"644"`, `"0644"`, `"1777"`.
- `ls -l` permission strings, optionally with the file type character: `"rw-r--r--"`, `"rwsr-xr-x"` (setuid), `"drwxrwxrwt"` (sticky).
- `chmod(1)` symbolic modes, applied to the empty mode `0000`: `"u=rw,go=r"`, `"a=rx,u+w"`, `"ug=rwx,o="`, `"u=rwxs,g=rx"`, `"a=rwx,+t"`. Without `u`, `g`, `o` or `a` a clause applies to all classes, and the umask is not applied. The copies `u`, `g` and `o` and the conditional `X` on the right-hand side are errors, as their result depends on an existing file.

Provider-defined functions need Terraform 1.8 or later, or OpenTofu 1.7 or later, and a `required_providers` entry for `blechschmidt/sysutils`; call it as `provider::sysutils::mode_to_octal(...)`. It is pure: it only parses its argument, never reads files or looks at the host, so its result is the same during plan and apply. Use `file()` or the [`sysutils_file`](../data-sources/file.md) data source to read the input.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Accept a mode in any notation and pass the octal form on.
variable "upload_dir_mode" {
  type    = string
  default = "u=rwx,g=rwxs,o="
}

resource "sysutils_directory" "uploads" {
  path = "/srv/app/uploads"
  mode = provider::sysutils::mode_to_octal(var.upload_dir_mode) # "2770"
}

data "sysutils_file" "shadow" {
  path = "/etc/shadow"
}

# Compare modes written in different notations.
check "shadow_not_world_readable" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.sysutils_file.shadow.mode != provider::sysutils::mode_to_octal("rw-r--r--")
    error_message = "/etc/shadow is world-readable."
  }
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
mode_to_octal(mode string) string
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `mode` (String) The mode in octal, `ls -l` or `chmod` symbolic notation.
